key_insight: MM-KG explicitly links multimodal patient evidence to biomedical knowledge graph relations, making clinical LLM inputs traceable, retrievable, and testable.
clinical_relevance: This could improve clinical question answering when both patient-specific data and external biomedical knowledge are needed, while separating useful evidence from irrelevant context.
method: Harmonize EHR text, imaging, genomics, and biospecimen data into typed observations mapped to UMLS concepts.
Align patient observations to a biomedical knowledge graph with explicit edges, then retrieve a compact query-specific subgraph.
Use the retrieved graph with either a large language model or a graph neural network for downstream prediction or ranking.
evidence_signal: Across MIMIC-IV and ADNI, combined patient evidence plus biomedical knowledge outperformed either source alone on interaction-heavy questions, with drug-controlled AUROC gains of +0.194 and +0.299, and retrieval used 6.8x less context at 0.731 AUROC.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate modality harmonization, concept mapping, and relation alignment, so performance may drop if upstream extraction or graph linkage is noisy.
paper_title: Aligning Multimodal Patient Evidence with Biomedical Knowledge Graphs for Clinical LLMs
